hobbies to become
frighteningly well read

a book club of two

read the same book as one friend each month and meet to talk about it. explaining what you thought out loud roughly doubles how much of a book you remember.

reading the classics

read one classic a season, slowly, a few pages every night. old books stretch your attention and your vocabulary in ways that modern ones very rarely do.

a daily lesson

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson about a new subject: art history, philosophy, astronomy. small daily doses build a mind that connects ideas effortlessly.

i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson about something new: art history, philosophy, astronomy. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and my mind connects ideas easily.

slides.texte_overlay:
visiting second hand bookshops

browse a second hand bookshop once a month and buy one book you'd never normally pick. surprising books lead to surprising thoughts, and those thoughts are what make people interesting.

writing in notebooks

keep a notebook for ideas, quotes and questions from everything you read. writing things down turns reading into thinking, and thinking into real intelligence.
